transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. It's nice to meet you too. Um, I came in because I've been taking on... well, just far more than I can realistically manage right now. 

I've started all these new projects, I'm doing workshops, I started making all these improvements to my studio, and I'm taking on constant client calls. It all just sort of piled up, and now the deadlines are all hitting at once, and the mortgage is starting to close in on me. I just realized I'm completely in over my head.
During this time, have you felt unusually energetic or driven compared with your normal self?

Yes, definitely. It was like... well, I had this humming current in me from the morning on. Sitting quietly felt almost impossible. So I just kept moving. I kept rearranging the studio, drafting new project proposals, emailing people, and fussing with all my art supplies. I just felt like I had to be doing something constantly.
During this period, did you need much less sleep than usual?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I was moving around a lot during the day, but I didn't really notice a change in my sleep. I still slept my normal amount... usually around seven or eight hours. I definitely still needed to rest at night, so I wouldn't say I needed less sleep than usual.
During this period, did you feel unusually confident or capable beyond your normal self?

Yes, I actually did. I started believing that my illustration work could become... well, the visual language that scientific journals had been missing for decades. And I felt oddly certain about it. I just felt like I was the one person who could actually pull it off.
At the time, did you believe you had a special or extraordinary ability that other people would find unrealistic?

Well, yes, like I just mentioned, I really thought my illustration work was going to revolutionize scientific journals. I felt completely convinced that I had this unique vision and that I was the only person capable of creating this new visual language for them. I suppose most people would think that sounds pretty unrealistic or overblown, but at the time, it just felt like a fact to me.
During this period, did you feel unusually cheerful or euphoric?

Yes, I did. Most days I felt... unusually buoyant, I guess you could say. Just really lit up. It felt like my studio and the garden were finally clicking into place. But it wasn't just cheerful all the time. I could actually snap pretty sharply at anyone who questioned my plans, or... well, if anyone asked me about invoices or things like that, I would get very short with them.
During this period, did you do anything unusually risky or impulsive for you?

Yes, I did. I ended up spending a lot of money that I didn't really have. I went out and bought a large-format printer, all these specialty papers, new lighting... even materials to renovate the studio. At the time, I just figured the money would sort itself out once my big breakthrough happened. It wasn't until later that I realized how much trouble I'd caused, financially speaking. I put my cottage-studio in a really precarious position.
How many days in a row did this unusually energized and buoyant period last?
Well, it was much longer than just a few days. It's actually been going on for about three months now. I'd say it started right around the time I took on the mortgage for the cottage-studio.
